questions.q: Why must the Israelites not sacrifice an ox or a sheep with any blemish or defect to Yahweh?
questions.a: A sacrifice that is not perfect will be detestable to Yahweh.

questions.q: What are the Israelites told to do if they hear that a man or woman within their cities have done what is evil in the sight of Yahweh and is serving other gods?
questions.a: The Israelites are to investigate thoroughly to know if this is true and that the idol worship is actually happening.

questions.q: What are the Israelites to do with a man or woman who has done such an evil thing as worshiping other gods?
questions.a: The Israelites are to stone that person to death.

questions.q: How many witnesses are needed to convict a person to death?
questions.a: Two or three witnesses are needed to convict a person to death.

questions.q: Who must throw the first stones when putting a person to death?
questions.a: The witnesses must be the first to throw the stones, followed by the rest of the people of Israel.

questions.q: Why must the Israelites stone the person to death who has done this evil action of worshiping other gods?
questions.a: This will get remove this evil from among them.

questions.q: Who is to judge if the Israelites have a matter that is too hard for them to judge?
questions.a: They must go to the place that Yahweh will choose, and explain the case to the Levites who are serving as priests and to the judge who is serving at that time and they will make the decision.

questions.q: What man must die in order to remove the evil from Israel?
questions.a: Anyone who acts arrogantly and does not listen to the decision of the priest or judge, must die to remove the evil from Israel.

questions.q: How will the Israelites decide who to set up as a king over them at the time when they are in the land?
questions.a: Israelites will select from among their fellow Israelites someone whom Yahweh will choose.

questions.q: Why must the king of Israel not own multiple horses, nor send anyone back to Egypt to buy more horses?
questions.a: He must not send anyone back to Egypt to buy more horses for him because Yahweh has told the Israelites to never return to Egypt.

questions.q: Why is the king told not to have many wives?
questions.a: He is not to marry a lot of wives because they might cause his heart to turn away from Yahweh.

questions.q: What is the king instructed to do so that he may learn to honor Yahweh his God, and keep and obey all of his law?
questions.a: He must write for himself a copy of this law on a scroll from which he is to read every day of his life.

questions.q: Why is the king instructed to keep the scroll of the law with him?
questions.a: He must read from the scroll daily so that he does not think he is more important than his fellow Israelites, and so that he will completely obey the commandments.

commentary.text: All sacrifices to be perfect, Idolaters must be slain.
The choice of a king, His duties.

Verses 1–7 No creature which had any blemish was to be offered in sacrifice to God. We are thus called to remember the perfect, pure, and spotless sacrifice of Christ, and reminded to serve God with the best of our abilities, time, and possession, or our pretended obedience will be hateful to him. So great a punishment as death, so remarkable a death as stoning, must be inflicted on the Jewish idolater. Let all who in our day set up idols in their hearts, remember how God punished this crime in Israel.

Courts of judgment were to be set up in every city. Though their judgment had not the Divine authority of an oracle, it was the judgment of wise, prudent, experienced men, and had the advantage of a Divine promise.

God himself was in a particular manner Israel's King; and if they set another over them, it was necessary that he should choose the person. Accordingly, when the people desired a king, they applied to Samuel, a prophet of the Lord. In all cases, God's choice, if we can but know it, should direct, determine, and overrule ours. Laws are given for the prince that should be elected. He must carefully avoid every thing that would turn him from God and religion. Riches, honours, and pleasures, are three great hinderances of godliness, (the lusts of the flesh, the lusts of the eye, and the pride of life,) especially to those in high stations; against these the king is here warned. The king must carefully study the law of God, and make that his rule; and having a copy of the Scriptures of his own writing, must read therein all the days of his life. It is not enough to have Bibles, but we must use them, use them daily, as long as we live. Christ's scholars never learn above their Bibles, but will have constant occasion for them, till they come to that world where knowledge and love will be made perfect. The king's writing and reading were as nothing, if he did not practise what he wrote and read. And those who fear God and keep his commandments, will fare the better for it even in this world.
